Subject: MedCipher — next steps & integration touchpoints

Hi Evan,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — really helpful to see the reranking flow and the constraints on latency for clinical lookup. Quick recap and a proposed set of next steps so we can scope the technical onboarding: 

Summary of needs you called out:
- Embeddings + reranker for candidate scoring (batch and nearline)
- Low-latency chat endpoint for clinician assist (p95 target: ~250ms)
- Controlled structured output for downstream ingestion (tool-calling / JSON schema)
- Data residency: all PHI stays in us-west; no EU egress

Open questions / asks for your team: 
1) Auth: do you prefer API keys behind a proxy or mTLS between services? If API keys, can you confirm rotation cadence and which proxy sits in front?
2) Sample data access: can you provision a sanitized sample payload and network CIDR so we can validate routing and throughput in our environment?
3) SOW/PO: finance/legal next steps — who should we loop in?

Proposed next steps from our side: 
- Technical setup call (60 min) to walk SDK setup, auth flow, and model-routing policy options — suggest Wed 04/19 10:00 PT or Thu 04/20 11:00 PT.
- Internal prework: we’ll assemble a short integration checklist and an initial model-routing proposal (latency vs cost tiers) and share it before the call.

I’ve attached a brief document describing your stated priorities (medcipher-integration-ambitions.xlsx). Ben and Karthik are copied to help with the technical follow-up.

Thanks — talk soon.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Solutions

Subject: Re: MedCipher — next steps & integration touchpoints

Evan —

Thanks for the diagram and answers. A few practical items to make the Wed call efficient: 

1) SDK & auth recommendation
- Use Redwood JS SDK for the clinician UI (examples here: https://redwood.ai/docs/sdk-js#auth).
- Auth pattern we prefer for proxy-managed API keys: short-lived signed tokens issued by a small service-account exchange (Token TTL ~ 5m) to avoid long-lived keys in clients. If your proxy rotates keys every 24h this meshes well — we can post a small exchange shim (Node) to run inside your VPC.

2) Model routing & fallback suggestion (initial proposal)
- Live Assist (latency-first route): route to quantized small-chat model on dedicated GPU pool (p95 budget <=250ms). If CPU/GPU saturated, fallback to a hosted lower-cost microservice variant with token-budget cap.
- Candidate generation (embeddings pipeline): run bulk embed jobs on a cost-optimized queue (batch GPUs) using redwood-embed-v1. Reranker: micro-batching to a medium-sized model for quality-sensitive scoring.
- Fallback chain example: embed batch -> reranker medium -> if reranker load > threshold, fall back to cached prefix reranker or lower-size model.

3) Structured output/tool-calling
- We'll surface a tool-calling contract: JSON schema for allowed tools, and a strict schema-with-validation step in the SDK before ingestion.
- For clinician actions (e.g., order lookup), we recommend defining a small set of explicit tools to avoid hallucination.

4) Region routing / data residency
- We'll pin the serving pool to us-west for any production tenant with PHI and add a region-routing policy to reject EU routing.

Prework I’ll post to the shared drive: an integration checklist and a one-page model-routing proposal. I attached a starter checklist (redwood-integration-checklist.xlsx). Also adding a sample Node token exchange snippet here for the call:

--- begin snippet ---
// minimal token exchange (Node)
app.post('/exchange', async (req, res) => {
  const saKey = process.env.SERVICE_ACCOUNT_KEY;
  // sign a short-lived token for client
  const token = signToken({ sub: 'medcipher-client' }, saKey, { expiresIn: '5m' });
  res.json({ token });
});
--- end snippet ---

Would you like us to include an initial proposed policy JSON in the drive before the call?

— Ben

Redwood Inference
